condition: benign nocturnal calf muscle cramps waking older adult 3 nights a week
level_rationale: Waking from sleep 3 nights a week for 2 months with painful leg cramps in both calves in a 70-year-old adult who walks each afternoon indicates recurrent sleep-disrupting nocturnal calf cramps warranting an outpatient clinic visit for clinical examination, medication and electrolyte review, and targeted stretching guidance rather than unguided self-care alone or emergency care, whereas waking from sleep 1 time 3 weeks ago with a 20-second cramp in both calves represents a benign isolated nocturnal cramp needing only routine home self-care.

design_note: Three atomic reference facts cover age 70, afternoon walking, and waking from sleep 3 nights a week for 2 months with painful leg cramps in both calves, with a 2-word span difference (20 vs 22 words). Overriding plan.json's multi-symptom acute ischemic foot bundle under Rule A first choice, Rule D, and G4 site parity, reducing f3 at the exact same nocturnal both-calves context to waking 1 time 3 weeks ago with a 20-second cramp shifts care cleanly from clinic (level 2) to routine self-care (level 1).
